_meta.purpose: Manual gate pilot for informed-reflection sentence classification (factual assertion vs speculative/hypothetical). Gold labels are human-judged by the pilot author BEFORE the rule set was run.

labels.FACTUAL: Declarative statement presenting something as true about the world; MUST be verified against the graph. A hedged wrapper does not change this if a checkable claim is being asserted.
labels.SPECULATIVE: Conditional, counterfactual, predictive, or explicitly opinion/imaginative content; not subject to fact-verification.
labels.MIXED: One sentence containing both a factual assertion AND speculative content (often in a single clause). Scored separately; a binary classifier cannot be 'correct' on these.

_meta.sourcing: Hand-authored representative examples over the system's actual subject domain (SpaceX, Tesla, LVMH, etc. from wiki_snapshots_v1). Per design.md section 2, the set DELIBERATELY over-samples hard cases (hedged-factual, mixed, speculative-definite). Aggregate accuracy is therefore a STRESS-TEST figure, not a population estimate.

sentences.text: SpaceX was founded by Elon Musk in 2002.
The Falcon 9 is a reusable launch vehicle developed by SpaceX.
LVMH owns Louis Vuitton.
Tesla is headquartered in Austin, Texas.
Larry Ellison co-founded Oracle.
The Nasdaq is a stock exchange located in New York City.
Neuralink develops brain-computer interfaces.
Blue Origin was founded by Jeff Bezos.
Louis Vuitton is a subsidiary of LVMH.
SpaceX develops rockets and spacecraft.
What if SpaceX had never been founded?
One might wonder whether Tesla could have succeeded without Musk.
If Blue Origin had launched first, the industry might look different today.
Perhaps reusable rockets will one day make spaceflight routine.
It is interesting to consider how LVMH might expand next.
SpaceX could eventually reach Mars within a decade.
One might argue that private spaceflight was inevitable.
Imagine a world where Oracle never existed.
Neuralink may transform medicine, though that remains uncertain.
I suspect the space industry will keep consolidating.
SpaceX was founded in 2002, and it might reach Mars within a decade.
LVMH owns Louis Vuitton, so perhaps it will acquire more luxury brands.
Tesla is based in Austin, and one wonders whether it will move again.
sentences.rationale: Assertion (based in Austin) + speculation (whether it will move).

sentences.text: Blue Origin was founded by Bezos, though it could have been anyone with capital.
sentences.rationale: Assertion (founded by Bezos) + counterfactual (could have been anyone).

sentences.text: The Falcon 9 is reusable, which suggests future rockets may be fully reusable too.
sentences.rationale: Assertion (Falcon 9 reusable) + speculation (future rockets may be).

sentences.text: Neuralink develops brain interfaces, and if it succeeds, medicine would change.
sentences.rationale: Assertion (develops) + conditional (if it succeeds ... would change).

sentences.text: It seems that SpaceX was founded in 2002.
sentences.rationale: Hedge wrapper ('it seems') but asserts a checkable fact that MUST be verified.

sentences.text: Perhaps the most important fact is that SpaceX develops rockets.
sentences.rationale: 'Perhaps' scopes the meta-judgment 'most important', not the embedded checkable claim 'SpaceX develops rockets'.

sentences.text: As far as I know, LVMH owns Louis Vuitton.
sentences.rationale: Epistemic hedge but asserts a checkable ownership fact.

sentences.text: If I recall correctly, Blue Origin was founded by Jeff Bezos.
sentences.rationale: 'If I recall' is a memory hedge, not a conditional over the world; the claim is checkable.

sentences.text: Apparently Tesla is headquartered in Austin.
sentences.rationale: Evidential hedge but asserts a checkable location fact.

sentences.text: There is no doubt that reusable rockets could fail catastrophically.
sentences.rationale: Definite framing ('no doubt') but the content 'could fail' is hypothetical, not a current fact.

sentences.text: Certainly, one could imagine SpaceX expanding to other planets.
sentences.rationale: Definite framing ('certainly') but content is imaginative.

sentences.text: It goes without saying that Musk founded SpaceX.
sentences.rationale: Definite framing over a checkable fact.

sentences.text: Undoubtedly, Neuralink develops brain-computer interfaces.
sentences.rationale: Definite framing over a checkable fact.

sentences.text: Clearly, the Falcon 9 is a reusable launch vehicle.
sentences.rationale: Definite framing over a checkable fact.

sentences.text: The luxury market will double in the next ten years.
sentences.rationale: Prediction about the future with no modal/hedge marker; not currently checkable.

sentences.text: Reusable rockets change the economics of spaceflight forever.
sentences.rationale: Sweeping editorial generalization ('forever'), present tense, no marker; not an atomic checkable claim.
